bullets.title: Applying International Safety and Infection-Prevention Standards
bullets.text: International healthcare systems expect nurses to translate policies and evidence into reliable clinical behaviour. While terminology and local procedures may vary, the underlying principles remain consistent: prevent avoidable harm, use standard precautions, assess risk, communicate clearly and practise within…

bullets.title: Clinical Risk Assessment and Early Escalation
bullets.text: International nursing practice places strong emphasis on recognising risk before harm occurs. Nurses are expected to combine structured assessment tools with clinical judgement, identify deterioration and escalate concerns using clear communication. A score or checklist supports judgement but does not replace it.

bullets.title: Safe Communication, Documentation and Incident Management
bullets.text: Communication failures contribute to many preventable incidents. Internationally qualified nurses must provide accurate handover, document care objectively, clarify uncertain instructions and report incidents through approved systems.
